runtime-alert-bot: [ALERT] runtime-integrity high confidence
Pod: prod/payment-worker-7bbcd
Node: gcp-us-west1-nd-07
Container: payments
Event: unexpected write to /host/proc/sysrq-trigger from /tmp/.suid
Score: 0.87
Logs:
```
<1769998739> openat(/host/proc/sysrq-trigger,O_WRONLY) = 3
<1769998740> write(3, \"1\", 1) = 1
```
Alert link: https://rwd-infra/alerts/ALERT-2026-03-20-1422

eric.infosec: Seeing a suspicious hostPath write from a container. Treating as potential container->host escape. I cordoned the node and evicted the pod. Created incident INC-2026-184. Assigning triage — please check tooling, image signature, and possible creds exposure.

bob.sre: Confirmed cordon+evict. Node gcp-us-west1-nd-07 cordoned at 1769998760. Evicted payment-worker-7bbcd. Taking cold snapshot of node now.

carlos.runtime: Pulled pod yaml from kube-apiserver before eviction:
```yaml
metadata:
  name: payment-worker-7bbcd
  namespace: prod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: payments
    image: registry.rwd.com/payments:v1.2.4
    securityContext:
      privileged: false
  volumes:
  - name: hostproc
    hostPath:
      path: /proc
      type: Directory
  automountServiceAccountToken: true
```
Note: tag v1.2.4 in registry currently has digest sha256:deadbeef... will verify signature.

alice.sec: Triage checklist (I'll start work):
1) Revoke SA tokens for that pod/namespace
2) Rotate any IAM creds/secrets the SA had access to
3) Verify image signature (cosign) and compare layer digests
4) Capture node forensic artifacts (/var/log, /proc, dmesg)
5) Enable/ensure kube-apiserver audit logging for pod exec, mounts, and writes
I'll take items 1 and 3 now.

dana.pm: :eyes: Any confirmed customer impact or data exfil? Payment jobs were running on that pod. We should prepare short internal + customer-safe comms.

eric.infosec: No confirmed exfil yet. The write target (/proc/sysrq-trigger) is suspicious — often used to trigger kernel behavior or persistence/backdoor attempts. Treat as potential escape attempt and escalate.

bob.sre: Actions run so far:
```
kubectl cordon gcp-us-west1-nd-07
kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep payment-worker-7bbcd
kubectl logs payment-worker-7bbcd -c payments --previous
# node snapshot
tar -czf /secure-archive/nd-07-$(date +%s)-snapshot.tgz /var/log /proc /etc
```
Also attached EBS/GCE disk snapshot for forensic analysis.

carlos.runtime: Registry check: digest matches what kube pulled, but cosign verification FAILED for tag v1.2.4 (no signature present). CI pushed that tag last week without signing. I'm pulling layers for offline inspection. Preliminary strings from /tmp/.suid show ELF that writes to /proc/sysrq-trigger and attempts to add keys to /tmp/.ssh/authorized_keys.

alice.sec: Done: revoked SA token and set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the payment-worker SA. Deleted any service-account secrets that could be used. Filed quick ticket to rotate AWS/GCP credentials attached to that SA. Also created immediate RBAC restrict binding to prevent pods in prod from using hostPath mounts to /proc and /sys while we finish triage.

eric.infosec: We should also rotate KMS wrapping keys and check KMS decrypt logs for this SA principal. I'm opening a KMS rotation request and will query cloud audit logs for decrypt operations in the last 72 hours. If any decrypts line up with suspicious timestamps, escalate to incident lead.

dana.pm: Communications plan: drafting internal update and a short customer-safe statement that says we detected suspicious activity, contained it, and are investigating. Will not go public yet.

bob.sre: Added admission webhook to block hostPath mounts targeting /proc and /sys across clusters (temporary). Also started enforcing PodSecurityAdmission (baseline -> restricted) for prod via canary rollout.

carlos.runtime: Forensic artifacts uploaded to secure bucket: gs://rwd-forensics/INC-2026-184/nd-07. Analysis shows potential persistence attempts and an outbound connection to 45.33.12.7 on port 443 from the host network namespace around the same time. Investigating egress logs and VPC flow logs.

alice.sec: If private keys are found, rotate them immediately. Commands I'm using to check KMS/audit:
```
# audit logs for decrypts by principal
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="svc-payments@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"' --freshness=72h
# list KMS operations
gcloud kms keys versions list --key=wrap-key --location=global --keyring=redwood-keys
```
Also drafting a new detection rule to alert on hostPath mounts to sensitive paths and on processes that call open/write against /host/proc.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-184 created and assigned to @eric.infosec; severity: P1. Runbook: https://rwd-ops/incidents/INC-2026-184/runbook

eric.infosec: Owners and next steps: bob.sre - node forensics and egress/VPC flows; carlos.runtime - image/layer analysis and cosign; alice.sec - RBAC/KMS rotation + detection rules; dana.pm - comms. Meeting at #incident-184 in 30m. Keep updates short here.
